matchstick.title: Compute numeric discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert each Roman numeral to its integer value, evaluate the left‑hand side and the right‑hand side (including operators), and compute the difference needed to balance the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of a matchstick puzzle, before trying any moves.
matchstick.example: For IV = XIV - V, LHS = 4, RHS = 14‑5 = 9, discrepancy = –5 (need to raise LHS by 5 or lower RHS by 5).

matchstick.title: Enumerate single‑stick numeral transformations
matchstick.principle: List all numeral changes achievable by moving a single stick while preserving its orientation, together with their numeric effect (e.g., V↔X changes value by ±5; I↔II changes by ±1).
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the discrepancy, to generate candidate moves.
matchstick.example: V → X adds 5, I → II adds 1; the reverse moves subtract the same amount.

matchstick.title: Validate source and destination characters
matchstick.principle: When a stick is removed from a character, the remaining sticks must still form a valid Roman numeral or operator; when a stick is added, the target must also become a valid character.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from V leaves a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral, so V→I is illegal.

matchstick.title: V↔X transformation (reposition diagonal)
matchstick.principle: Reposition one diagonal stick of a V so it crosses the other, turning V (5) into X (10) or vice versa; this changes the value by ±5 while keeping both characters valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the needed numeric adjustment is exactly 5 (or –5).
matchstick.example: Changing the V in IV to X yields IX, turning 4 into 9.

matchstick.title: I↔II vertical addition/removal
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to an I creates II (value +1); removing a vertical stick from II yields I (value –1).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy is ±1 and a vertical stick is available.
matchstick.example: Turning I into II raises the left side from 1 to 2.

matchstick.title: Operator change: – to + (or + to –)
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to a minus sign creates a plus sign, turning subtraction into addition (RHS changes by +2 × right operand); removing a vertical from a plus makes a minus (RHS changes by –2 × right operand).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy equals twice the right‑hand operand (or its negative).
matchstick.example: Changing ‘‑ V’ to ‘+ V’ adds 10 to the RHS (2 × 5).

matchstick.title: Never alter the equality sign
matchstick.principle: The ‘=’ sign must stay as two horizontal sticks; moving a stick away destroys the equality operator and makes the equation invalid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: For any candidate move that involves the ‘=’ sign.
matchstick.example: Removing one horizontal from ‘=’ would turn it into ‘‑’, which is not allowed.

matchstick.title: Respect stick orientation
matchstick.principle: Angled (diagonal) sticks cannot serve as vertical sticks; a diagonal cannot be used to form an I after removal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering transformations that would change a diagonal into a vertical or vice versa.
matchstick.example: Taking a diagonal from V does not produce a valid I.

matchstick.title: Re‑evaluate arithmetic after each move
matchstick.principle: After applying a candidate stick move, recompute the numeric values to confirm the equality holds; discard moves that are visually plausible but numerically false.
matchstick.example: After turning V into X, check that 4 = 14 – 10 indeed holds.

matchstick.title: Prefer intra‑character stick repositioning
matchstick.principle: Moving a stick within the same character (e.g., V→X) often yields a valid solution without affecting other characters, reducing the risk of creating invalid source or target symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the needed numeric change matches the effect of an intra‑character transformation.
matchstick.example: Instead of taking a stick from another numeral, simply reposition a diagonal in the V to make X.

matchstick.description: Treating a diagonal stick as a vertical I
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model forgets that stick orientation is fixed, assuming any stick can become an I after removal.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Remember that angled sticks cannot be used as vertical sticks; only vertical sticks can form I.

matchstick.why_it_happens: Attempting to use the ‘=’ sign as a source of sticks, which would break the required equality operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never move sticks away from or onto ‘=’; it must remain two horizontal sticks.

matchstick.description: Leaving an invalid source character after removal
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick without checking whether the remaining shape still matches a valid Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always verify that the character you take a stick from remains a valid symbol after the removal.

matchstick.why_it_happens: Focusing solely on numeral changes and overlooking that changing a minus to a plus (or vice versa) can resolve the discrepancy.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Include operator changes in the list of possible single‑stick moves and evaluate their numeric impact.

matchstick.description: Skipping arithmetic verification after a visual change
matchstick.why_it_happens: Relying on the appearance of a corrected equation without recomputing its numeric value.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Re‑calculate the left‑ and right‑hand side values after every candidate move to ensure the equality truly holds.
